claim: The checked-in browser assertions now test the declared map field and backing projection and retain explicit reading/overflow checks, rather than expecting the removed square, content-fitted map and portrait-only field variants. This does not close the overall requested format invariant.
evidence: Both updated Python browser scripts compile locally. Their exact blob SHAs match the temporary experiment at 654a5ff0: membrane 404513332d2f66fdac3e700981793a995b1f8efd; bounded b3155151bfa820d5133bf3732175d25b006e63a2.

In the browser grid-probe run https://github.com/QuantumCephalopod/cambium/actions/runs/42741743565, the updated membrane-grid step passed 18 site/viewport cases. The experiment also contained a narrower headerContent field; the outer and map declarations were unchanged. This is not a browser run of the exact product head.

The updated bounded-layout step found horizontal header overflow at 390 by 844 in the experimental narrower-header variant (clientWidth 49, scrollWidth 58). That experiment is not in the product branch. This is an unresolved design and readability finding, not proof that the exact product-head header has the same overflow.
A prior bounded-layout run against the earlier header placement also encountered a header clearance assertion; it compared a container boundary, so it does not by itself prove glyph clipping.
open: Resolve and rerun the actual product header reading/overflow checks in both orientations using a real browser, without speculative CSS fitting or changing the authored outer cells.
